summary.en: Pakistani security forces continued raids on TTP hideouts, killing dozens of militants in separate operations, while police thwarted a major terror attack in Lakki Marwat, killing a suspected suicide bomber. A Pakistani minister travelled to India for a SCO meeting, marking the first ministerial visit since the 2025 war, and senior military commander CDF Munir was briefed on operations in Balochistan. Civilian casualties rose after two separate bus-gas tanker collisions killed ten people each, and a strike shut down activity across Balochistan. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker fortsatte raid på TTP-skjulesteder, og drepte dusinvis av militante i separate operasjoner, mens politiet avverget et stort terrorangrep i Lakki Marwat, og drepte en mistenkt selvmordsbomber. En pakistansk minister reiste til India for et SCO-møte, den første ministerbesøket siden krigen i 2025, og den høytstående militærkommandøren CDF Munir ble informert om operasjoner i Balochistan. Sivile tap økte etter to separate kollisjoner mellom buss og gass tanker som drepte ti personer hver, og et streik stengte ned aktivitet over hele Balochistan. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
